text: At 2,150 m in the Barail sandstone interval, a gas influx of approximately 0.8 m³ was detected. Pit gain monitoring showed a 0.8 m³ increase over 15 minutes. SIDPP registered 280 psi, SICP 320 psi. Well was immediately shut-in on the annular preventer. Driller's method kill procedure was initiated using 1.44 SG kill mud. Kill completed after 6 hours. Subsequent mud weight maintained at 1.44 SG for continued drilling. Barail Group formation pressure in this sector estimated at equivalent mud weight 1.38–1.42 SG. Recommend all offset well plans in this area carry minimum 0.08 SG kick margin above pore pressure gradient.

Partial mud losses of approximately 3 m³/hour encountered at 950 m in the Tipam Sandstone formation. The loss zone appears to be associated with a high-permeability channel sandstone. Surface pit levels dropped 2.5 m³ before losses were identified. LCM treatment was prepared using 30 ppb fine mica and 10 ppb graphite flakes. LCM pill of 20 m³ pumped at reduced rate. Losses reduced to less than 0.5 m³/hour within 4 hours. Drilling continued with elevated LCM concentration in active mud system. Tipam Sandstone at 900–1,050 m depth range in the DLJ block is consistently porous and permeable. Pre-treatment with LCM is recommended when approaching this interval.

Severe stuck pipe incident occurred at 3,120 m depth in the Barail Group shale interbed sequence. The drill string became immobile during a connection, suggesting torsional or key-seat sticking mechanism. Overpull of 45 kN applied with no pipe movement. Jar down sequence initiated after 2 hours of attempts. A 15 m³ oil-based spotting pill was pumped to the stuck point. After 8 hours, the jars fired and the string was freed with 32 kN overpull. Total NPT 28 hours. BHA inspection on surface revealed wear on drill collar stabiliser. No fish left in hole. The Barail shale interbed at 3,080–3,200 m has been identified as a high-risk sticking zone in multiple DLJ wells. Recommend lubricity additives in mud program and torque/drag monitoring when approaching this depth.

Critical gas influx encountered at 4,100 m in the Sylhet Limestone formation during drilling at NKT-01. Pit gain was 2.4 m³ over 10 minutes. SIDPP measured 680 psi, SICP 720 psi. Emergency shut-in executed on ram BOP. Formation pressure gradient calculated at 1.62 SG equivalent. Heavyweight kill mud (1.65 SG) prepared and bullheaded against formation. Kill operations took 18 hours due to fracture-induced fluid losses complicating wellbore pressure management. After successful kill, extra intermediate liner string (7") was run to isolate the overpressured Kopili Shale before drilling into Sylhet Limestone. This incident established the baseline that Sylhet Limestone in the Naharkatiya sector is highly overpressured (1.55–1.65 SG pore pressure equivalent). Operators drilling to Sylhet targets must plan for heavyweight mud systems and have contingency casing strings in well design.

Total lost circulation at 2,450 m depth in the Barail Group fractured sandstone interval. Mud returns lost entirely at surface. Pumps were shut down as a precautionary measure. The loss zone was identified as a natural fracture system in the Barail Group. An LCM treatment consisting of 85 m³ of coarse and fine blended material was pumped in stages. A cement squeeze was performed at the loss zone. Circulation was partially restored after 48 hours. Drilling resumed with drill-water until LCM circulation was confirmed. Multiple cement plugs were placed before the loss zone was bridged. This zone at 2,400–2,500 m in the NKT field should be pre-planned with standby LCM stock of minimum 100 m³ and a contingency cement plug procedure in the well program.

Total lost circulation at 3,420 m in highly fractured Barail sandstone interval at NKT-04. Complete mud loss with no returns at surface. Caliper log confirmed cavernous zone of approximately 0.6 m washout. A total of 85 m³ LCM material (coarse shell, medium mica, graphite) pumped over 72 hours with intermittent cement plugs. Drill water used to maintain hydrostatic column during cure time. Multiple cement plugs placed to bridge the cavern. Circulation partially restored after 72 hours. Well had to be sidetracked above loss zone and 9⅝" casing set at 3,380 m to isolate. This confirms a consistent fractured zone at 3,350–3,450 m in the Barail Group across the NKT sector. Pre-emptive casing shoe at 3,380 m recommended in all future NKT area wells targeting Sylhet Limestone.

Drill string became stuck at 3,520 m in the Kopili Shale formation at LKW-01. Differential sticking mechanism suspected due to high ECD and depleted formation zone. Overpull of 45 kN applied with no pipe movement. A 10 m³ oil-based spotting pill was pumped. Slow rotation applied with top drive. KCl/Polymer mud system changeover initiated during stuck pipe remediation to improve shale inhibition. After 22 hours, the pipe was freed with 38 kN overpull. Backreamed to casing shoe. Wellbore stabilisation measures adopted including reduced mud weight window monitoring and ECD management. The Kopili Shale in the Lakwa sector (3,450–3,700 m depth range) is identified as a highly reactive swelling shale formation. Inhibitive mud systems (KCl/Polymer or OBM) are mandatory for drilling this interval. Maximum mud weight must account for borehole creep tendency.

Second stuck pipe incident at LKW-01 in the Kopili Shale interval, this time at 3,640 m, just 18 days after the previous event at 3,520 m. The recurring nature of sticking events in this well across the Kopili interval (3,450–3,700 m) indicates systematic wellbore instability driven by shale swelling and borehole ellipticity. Despite KCl/Polymer mud implementation after the first event, the second sticking required 18 hours of jar work and PHPA pill spotting to free. A total of 62 hours NPT was incurred across both stuck pipe incidents in this well. Post-well review recommended full OBM system for future wells drilling through Kopili Shale below 3,400 m. Casing plan was revised to include an additional liner string to reduce open-hole exposure in this interval.

Severe mud losses encountered at 1,380 m in the Tipam Sandstone during drilling of DLJ-02. Losses escalated from partial (4 m³/hr at 1,100 m) to total (18 m³/hr) within 6 hours of continued drilling. Surface mud volumes dropped 45 m³ before recognition and shut-down. A primary LCM treatment of 40 m³ was pumped, followed by a cement plug. Despite initial control, losses recurred when drilling resumed. A sidetrack was drilled around the primary loss zone. A second cement plug was placed and successfully bridged the secondary loss path. Total NPT for this event: 36 hours. Lesson learned: once partial losses are encountered in Tipam Sandstone at DLJ, reduce penetration rate by 50% and increase LCM concentration in mud system before attempting to drill ahead. Do not pump losses below 2 m³/hr threshold without LCM pre-treatment.

Total lost circulation at 1,240 m in cavernous Tipam Sandstone zone at RDG-03. This was identified as a karst-like cave system within the Tipam formation based on caliper logging. Returns were completely lost, and no LCM treatment was effective in this stage. A cement plug was set and the wellbore was sidetracked. The sidetrack also encountered partial losses at 1,265 m, indicating a laterally extensive fracture/cave network. A second cement plug and LCM blend were used. Drilling resumed with drill water until full mud returns were established at 1,310 m. Total NPT: 60 hours. This is now a known hazard zone at 1,200–1,300 m in the RDG block. A pre-emptive casing shoe at approximately 1,180 m should be considered in well programs for RDG area wells to isolate this zone.

Cement bond log (CBL/VDL) run on NKT-02 after setting 9⅝" casing at 2,550 m revealed poor bond quality across the 2,050–2,150 m interval in the Barail Group formation. Amplitude readings on CBL indicated 70–80% free pipe in this 100 m interval. A micro-annulus was suspected due to pressure differential during cement curing. The poor bond zone corresponds to a gas-bearing Barail sandstone, creating a potential gas migration risk. Squeeze cementing operation was planned and executed: 4 m³ of neat cement squeezed at maximum pressure 800 psi. Post-squeeze CBL showed improved bond across most of the interval, with residual questionable bond at 2,095–2,110 m. Deferred for production monitoring. Lesson: use centraliser programme with minimum 70% standoff in Barail gas-bearing sands. Consider lightweight spacer before cement to improve mud displacement.

Critical well control event at DHJ-01 during drilling at 3,980 m in the Sylhet Limestone formation. A major gas influx of 2.1 m³ was detected during a connection. SIDPP=720 psi, SICP=780 psi. Formation pressure gradient calculated at 1.65 SG equivalent, exceeding pre-drill prognosis of 1.55 SG by 0.10 SG. Emergency procedures activated. BOP closed on ram preventers. Kill mud weight of 1.68 SG prepared using heavyweight barite. Bullheading performed. Kill operations required 12 hours due to fracture system allowing partial circulation. Post-kill, casing shoe integrity confirmed. Extra liner string (5") run to 4,150 m with high-density cement (1.95 SG). The Sylhet Limestone in the Dohali area is now classified as a high-pressure, high-risk target requiring enhanced well control procedures, additional casing strings, and heavyweight mud contingency plans.

Gas kick event recorded at DLJ-05 at 2,890 m in the Barail Group sandstone. Pit gain of 1.2 m³ detected during drilling with flow check showing positive flow. SIDPP=310 psi, SICP=365 psi. Well shut-in on annular BOP. Driller's method kill initiated. Kill mud at 1.42 SG circulated (two circulation cycles). Well successfully killed in 6 hours. Post-kill monitoring showed stable well conditions. Mud weight raised to 1.44 SG for continued drilling. Gas analysis from kick fluid showed C1 dominant (dry gas), confirming Barail Group as source. This event, combined with the DLJ-01 kick at 2,150 m, establishes a Barail Group pore pressure gradient of 1.38–1.42 SG across the DLJ area. Well plans must account for overpressure in the 2,700–3,000 m Barail sandstone interval.

Significant gas influx at NKT-01 during drilling at 3,180 m in the Kopili Shale formation. Pit gain of 1.8 m³ detected over 20 minutes while rotating off-bottom. SIDPP=480 psi, SICP=520 psi. Formation pressure gradient at this depth: 1.48 SG equivalent. This was higher than the planned 1.42 SG mud weight. Well was shut-in. Bullhead procedure selected due to well geometry. Kill mud of 1.52 SG used. Kill operations took 12 hours. The Kopili Shale in the Naharkatiya sector has been confirmed as overpressured in this depth range (3,100–3,250 m). Post-incident review recommended an additional casing string to isolate Kopili Shale before drilling into the Sylhet Limestone target. This recommendation was implemented in NKT-04 well design.

Gas shows encountered during drilling at 2,340 m in the Barail Group sandstone at HLG-01. Pit gain of 0.6 m³ was noted over 30 minutes. Background gas levels increased from 2% to 18% total gas. SIDPP=180 psi after flow check. Mud weight was increased progressively from 1.34 SG to 1.38 SG in stages while circulating. Well was monitored continuously. No full BOP shut-in was required. Gas levels returned to baseline within 4 hours. Drilling resumed at reduced penetration rate. The Barail Group at HLG field shows moderate overpressure in the 2,250–2,450 m depth range with pore pressure equivalent approximately 1.35–1.38 SG. Mud weight of 1.38 SG provides adequate overbalance for this area.

Differential sticking event at RDG-01 at 2,980 m in the Barail Group formation. Drill string became immobile during a pipe connection. Overpull of 30 kN was applied. A 5 m³ oil-based spotting pill was pumped to the stuck point using a combination of drill pipe displacement and reverse circulation. Slow rotation was applied with the top drive at 20 RPM to maintain torsional movement. After 14 hours, the pipe became free with a jarring sequence. The pipe was backreamed to surface for BHA inspection. Wear marks on stabilisers confirmed key-seat sticking in a sand-shale transition zone. Recommend using lubricating mud additives (minimum 1% lubricant by volume) when drilling through the Barail Group below 2,800 m in the RDG area. Maintain minimum flow rate to avoid formation contact.

Seepage-level mud losses of 1.2 m³/hour encountered at 3,200 m in the fractured Kopili Shale at DLJ-01. Caliper log indicated minor borehole enlargement at this depth. LCM treatment was applied with fine bridging agents. Mud viscosity was increased from 42 to 55 seconds funnel viscosity to improve bridging efficiency. Losses were controlled within 6 hours and drilling resumed. The Kopili Shale between 3,100–3,300 m in the DLJ area shows consistent micro-fracturing that can cause seepage to partial losses. A proactive approach of pre-treating mud with fine LCM before entering this formation is recommended. The losses in Kopili Shale do not typically escalate to severe losses unless high ECD conditions are maintained.

Partial mud losses of 6 m³/hour encountered at 2,440 m in the Barail Group fracture zone at LKW-02. The loss zone correlated with a seismic-identified fault at this location. LCM treatment with fine-medium mix was pumped. Two-stage cementing was planned for the subsequent 9⅝" casing string to account for these losses. Drilling continued with reduced ROP and managed pressure approach. The Barail Group fracture zone in the LKW area at 2,400–2,500 m correlates with regional fault trends mapped by 3D seismic. Wells in this area should have pre-planned cementing programs that account for cement loss into fractures. Foam cement or lightweight cement plugs prior to slurry pumping may help establish a bridging base.

Severe lost circulation event at 1,240 m in a high permeability Tipam Sandstone channel sand body at NKT-04. Losses were 28 m³/hour — full mud returns lost within minutes of entering the zone. This channel sand is interpreted as a direct connection to a highly permeable reservoir. LCM pills were pumped but ineffective. A cement plug was set to bridge the zone. Drilling resumed with water-based drilling fluid until losses could be controlled. A subsequent cement plug stabilised the wellbore. This loss zone at 1,180–1,300 m in the NKT area corresponds to a known regional high-porosity/permeability Tipam channel. Pre-emptive casing at 1,180 m is strongly recommended for future NKT wells to avoid this issue.

Seepage mud losses encountered at 2,440 m in a fractured Barail sandstone interval in DLJ-04. Losses were approximately 2.5 m³/hour. LCM concentration was increased in the active mud system. The wellbore was monitored closely as this depth corresponded to a potential kick zone. Losses self-healed after 8 hours of managed drilling. The coincidence of a loss zone and an overpressured Barail sand in this area creates a narrow mud weight window — overbalance creates losses, underbalance risks influx. Managed pressure drilling techniques or at minimum, a real-time ECD monitoring protocol should be used in this interval (2,350–2,500 m) in DLJ area wells.

Torque spikes observed at the Girujan-Tipam formation boundary at approximately 850 m in DLJ-03. Torque fluctuated between 8 and 15 kN·m compared to a baseline of 10 kN·m in the Girujan Clay above. The transition zone shows alternating hard and soft layers that cause BHA vibration. RPM was reduced from 140 to 90 and WOB adjusted down by 20%. Lubricity additive (10 m³ lubricant pill) was circulated. Torque stabilised within 2 hours at 10 kN·m. The Girujan-Tipam transition in the DLJ block at 780–870 m consistently shows this behaviour. Pre-drilling BHA design should account for vibration dampening in this interval. Anti-vibration subs or PDM in anti-whirl mode recommended.

Torque spikes were recorded at 1,480 m in the Tipam Sandstone at MKM-01. The spikes coincide with coal stringer intercalations identified on gamma ray logs. Coal stringers at 1,440–1,520 m show GR values >120 API and high resistivity. The hard coal layers cause bit bounce and torque fluctuations. Parameters were optimised: RPM 80, WOB 12 kN, flow rate 24 l/s. ROP was reduced from 10 to 6 m/hr to manage vibrations. The coal stringer interval at MKM was drilled without significant NPT. Coal stringer intervals in the Tipam-Barail transition are a recognised feature across the Upper Assam Basin. Bit selection (PDC with high number of cutters) helps in reducing vibrations across coal-bearing intervals.

Intermittent torque spikes observed at 3,200 m in the Kopili Shale at NKT-02. Torque varied 12–20 kN·m. Suspected clay balling of BHA. PHPA/KCl pill of 8 m³ was circulated. Reaming passes performed across the high-drag section. Shale cuttings analysis indicated significant swelling tendency of Kopili Clay minerals (smectite content 35–40%). PHPA mud addition helped suppress swelling. After treatment, torque stabilised at 13 kN·m and drilling continued normally. Kopili Shale at 3,100–3,400 m depth in NKT area consistently shows high clay content and swelling tendency. PHPA concentration minimum 1.5 kg/m³ and KCl at 5% by weight are recommended mud specifications for drilling this interval.

Torque fluctuations observed at 2,890 m in the Kopili Shale at HLG-01. Erratic torque 10–18 kN·m for a sustained 4-hour period. Clay balling suspected on bit and BHA stabilisers. PHPA mud sweep pumped. Wiper trip performed from 2,890 m to 2,700 m. Drag was noted on the first stand but reduced progressively. On return to bottom, torque was stable at 12 kN·m. The Kopili Shale in HLG area (2,850–3,200 m) has similar reactive characteristics to the NKT sector. Mud inhibition is key. Monitoring of cuttings returns to identify shale reactivity early is recommended. Any balling indication should trigger immediate circulating pill.

Small gas influx of 0.4 m³ encountered at 3,580 m in the Kopili Shale at DLJ-04. The influx was detected during a survey stop. SIDPP=180 psi upon shut-in. Driller's method used with kill mud of 1.46 SG. Kill completed in 4 hours. This small kick, combined with the larger event at NKT-01 at similar depth, suggests overpressure in Kopili Shale is present across a regional extent in the eastern part of the DLJ block. Formation pressure equivalent mud weight in the Kopili Shale here is 1.42–1.46 SG. Mud weight of 1.48 SG recommended when drilling Kopili Shale in DLJ area to maintain adequate overbalance. The narrow mud weight window (fracture gradient 1.54 SG) limits options.

Gas influx of 0.7 m³ at LKW-02 at 3,850 m while drilling through the Kopili Shale. SIDPP=210 psi after shut-in on annular. Driller's method selected. Kill mud of 1.46 SG circulated for 5 hours. Well killed successfully. Post-kill, mud weight maintained at 1.48 SG. This event, correlated with LKW-01 data and NKT area kicks, confirms regional Kopili Shale overpressure in the 3,500–4,000 m depth range. A minimum 1.46 SG mud weight is recommended for Kopili Shale drilling in the LKW and NKT sectors. Formation integrity test data from multiple wells indicates fracture gradient is 1.58 SG at this depth, providing a narrow but workable mud weight window.

MWD/LWD tool failure at NKT-03 at 2,450 m caused 18 hours NPT. The GR-resistivity tool assembly short-circuited during circulation. The string was pulled to surface and the tool assembly replaced. Fishing was not required. Possible causes: shock and vibration damage from Tipam-Barail transition zone (encountered approximately 100 m above failure depth). Post-run analysis showed high vibration signatures preceding failure. Recommend using shock sub in BHA assembly when drilling through the Tipam-Barail transition zone (1,800–2,100 m). Vibration data from surface measurements should be monitored in real time. Tool failures in the 2,400–2,600 m range in NKT area have been noted in multiple wells, often correlated with the transition zone vibration environment.

Packoff incident at RDG-03 at 3,050 m while tripping in the Kopili Shale section. Drill string encountered resistance and then became immobile. An overpull of 25 kN was applied. Pipe was worked with slow rotation and reciprocation. Circulation was established after clearing a packoff with cuttings. The string was freed after 8 hours of working. Analysis indicated cuttings accumulation in the borehole — inadequate hole cleaning during the previous drilling run. Minimum annular velocity of 0.6 m/s must be maintained in Kopili Shale sections. Wiper trips before tripping in are mandatory in wells with known balling tendency. This applies to all RDG area wells drilling in the Kopili interval (3,000–3,800 m).

Minor seepage losses of 1 m³/hour at 920 m in the Tipam Sandstone at NKT-02. The self-sealing nature of fine-grained sandstone at this depth allowed the losses to reduce without active LCM treatment. Fine LCM was added to the mud system as a precautionary measure. Drilling continued without significant interruption. This event, while minor, is consistent with the pattern of Tipam Sandstone seepage losses noted across NKT and DLJ area wells in the 850–1,100 m depth range. Proactive maintenance of 10 ppb fine LCM in the active mud system when drilling Tipam Sandstone is a cost-effective preventive measure that eliminates the need for reactive LCM treatments.

Torque spikes observed at 1,680 m in the Tipam Sandstone at RDG-02. The spikes (8–16 kN·m baseline 10 kN·m) coincide with interbedded shale-sandstone couplets identified on the gamma ray log. WOB was reduced from 15 to 10 kN and RPM adjusted from 120 to 95 RPM. Reaming pass of 3 stands was performed. Torque stabilised at 11 kN·m after parameter optimisation. Drilling continued without further events. The Tipam interbedded sequence in the RDG area between 1,600–1,800 m is characterised by abrupt lithology changes that can cause BHA vibration and torque fluctuations. Running a PDM in the BHA at this depth range with controlled WOB is recommended to minimise vibration events.

Key-seat sticking event at DLJ-01 at 2,480 m while pulling out of hole in the Barail Group formation. The key-seat formed in a deviation build section where dog-leg severity was 1.8°/30m. Overpull of 15 kN applied. Surfactant-based spotting pill was circulated. After working the string for 4 hours, the pipe was freed. Backreamed through the key-seat zone. The combination of Barail Group lithological contrasts and wellbore deviation is a trigger for key-seat formation. In deviated wells, key-seat wiper subs should be included in BHA design when drilling through the Barail Group in areas with planned inclinations above 10°. Torque and drag modelling should be calibrated against actual data in real time.

Mud losses at 2,450 m in the Barail Group at DHJ-01. Losses were 7 m³/hour, consistent with a fracture-dominated loss zone. LCM treatment with medium nut plug and graphite was prepared and pumped as a 15 m³ pill. Losses reduced to 2 m³/hour after treatment. Continued drilling with lower penetration rate. This Barail Group fracture zone at DHJ correlates with the mapped regional fault structure. Losses at 2,350–2,550 m in DHJ area are consistently seen in wells approaching this fault. Pre-treatment with proactive LCM before entering this depth range and having a cement plug procedure on standby are recommended.

High torque of 22 kN·m recorded at 3,200 m in the Kopili Shale at DHJ-01, significantly above the normal 13 kN·m baseline. Clay balling suspected on bit and lower BHA. PHPA mud pill of 10 m³ circulated. Reaming trips from 3,200 m to 3,100 m performed twice. Post-reaming torque stabilised at 14 kN·m. The DHJ area Kopili Shale (3,100–3,600 m) shows high clay content similar to NKT and LKW areas. Mud chemistry must be maintained with fresh KCl concentration checks every 8 hours. Cuttings volume and shape monitoring is essential for early balling detection. High torque in this formation should trigger a circulating pill before balling becomes established.

During cementing of 9⅝" casing at LKW-02, cement returns were lost at 2,300–2,350 m during the displacement phase. The loss zone corresponded to a fractured Kopili Shale section identified on the pre-drill seismic. A micro-annulus is suspected in the 2,300–2,350 m interval. CBL run 48 hours post-cementing showed partial bond (60% amplitude) in this zone. A squeeze cement job was planned. 3.5 m³ neat cement squeezed at 750 psi maximum. Post-squeeze CBL improved to 80% bond across most of the zone. Residual questionable bond at 2,315–2,330 m. Deferred for production monitoring. Lesson: pre-planned cement programs for Kopili Shale casing should use a light lead cement followed by a heavier tail to better fill fractures.

Partial mud losses of 8 m³/hour encountered at 2,200 m in a fracture zone in the Barail Group at RDG-03. This fracture zone was predicted from 3D seismic interpretation as a secondary fault splay. Bridging agent and graphite LCM pill was pumped as a 12 m³ treatment. Losses reduced to 1.5 m³/hour after treatment. A second smaller LCM pill was pumped after 6 hours and losses reduced to seepage. Drilling continued at reduced penetration rate (4 m/hr vs normal 8 m/hr). The Barail Group fracture network in the RDG area is seismically mapped and shows multiple splay faults in the 2,100–2,400 m depth range. Planned entry into these fracture zones should be preceded by LCM pre-treatment and reduced penetration rate approach.
